note: EDIT THIS FILE to add a model. No code change is needed. scripts/loop/model_router.py reads it at every call, validates it, and refuses to run on a malformed entry rather than silently ignoring it. Adding a row is how a new OpenRouter model, a new Codex model or a new Claude tier enters the loop.
fields: DERIVED VIEWS (FX-31.6): every model table the loop once typed by hand is a projection of these rows, built by scripts/loop/model_router.py derive_model_views and checked by scripts/loop/registry_measure.py. Optional row fields: `aliases` (extra bridge CLI names for this row, the row's own name is always one), `spoken` (phrases the owner types at intake that mean this row), `answers_as` (the id the bridge's [usage] line reports when it differs from `id`, which the strict dispatcher compares against), `arm` ({keys, cost_usd, mix}: the ledger substrings that read as this build arm, its USD per build, and its share of the default worker mix). `fallback` (true on a bridge row the bridge itself tries, in row order, after the requested model fails: or_ask FALLBACK_MODELS), `stage` (seated when absent; retired or shadow never seat anywhere the loop builds a seating list: chain, the worker mix, the repair wave, the fan out's job allowlist and the dispatch aliases all read seated rows only, while the bridge itself may still reach the row as its own fallback). `read_on` at the top is the date the rows were last measured; registry_measure.py --check warns past 90 days and blocks nothing.
read_on_note: the date of the newest MEASURED note below (sonnet55_live); not a guess. registry_measure.py --check reads it.

quality_is_an_unmeasured_prior: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE ORDER. Every `quality` number in this file is a PRIOR typed by hand on 2026-09-21, not a measurement. No benchmark on this estate has scored these models against each other for build, grade, prose or plan. They are stated as estimates rather than dressed up as data, because a ranking presented as measured when it is guessed is the fabrication this estate forbids absolutely. The MEASURED term is `reliability`, which model_router.py reads from the outcome ledger and which outranks cost within a quality tier. It returned nothing until 2026-09-21, because no outcome row carried a model id anywhere on this estate; record_outcome() now writes one on every call, so this prior gets corrected by evidence as the ledger fills. Until then, treat the order as a starting guess that is cheap to change: edit a number here, no code change, no deploy.
